title.rendered: How to Get Apple Student Discount (And What You’ll Actually Save)

content.rendered:
Apple devices rarely go on sale, but students, teachers, and school staff can get year-round savings on select products through the official Apple Education Store. And for a limited time each year, Apple runs a Back to School promotion that adds even more value, often throwing in AirPods or an Apple Pencil for free.

If you’re wondering how it all works and how much you’ll actually save in 2026, here’s everything you need to know—explained in simple, clear terms.

Table of Contents
  • What Apple Products Are Discounted for Students?
  • How Much Can You Save with Apple's Education Discount?
    • iPad Discounts (U.S. Pricing)
    • Mac & MacBook Discounts (U.S. Pricing)
  • Who's Eligible for the Apple Student Discount?
  • How Apple Verifies Eligibility (By Region)
  • Apple Education Store Purchase Limits
  • How to Get the Student Discount
  • Apple's Back to School Offer
  • Bonus: Apple Music Student Plan
  • Final Tip

What Apple Products Are Discounted for Students?

Student discounts apply only to a few product categories:

  • MacBook Air and MacBook Pro
  • iMac and Mac mini
  • iPad Air and iPad Pro

You won’t get a discount on iPhones, Apple Watch, Apple TV, HomePods, accessories, or software. AirPods, Magic Mouse, Apple Pencil, and other accessories aren’t directly discounted either, but Apple often gives them away during their annual Back to School deal.

How Much Can You Save with Apple’s Education Discount?

Apple doesn’t follow a fixed percentage discount. Instead, the savings vary based on the model and region. But here’s a general idea:

  • Up to $200 off on Macs
  • Up to $100 off on iPads

Here’s how regular prices compare to student pricing in the U.S.

iPad Discounts (U.S. Pricing)

Mac & MacBook Discounts (U.S. Pricing)

Apple offers similar education pricing in the U.K., Canada, Australia, India, and other regions. The exact prices vary by country and local currency, but the savings typically fall in the same range: around 10–15% off on eligible iPads and Macs.

Who’s Eligible for the Apple Student Discount?

To qualify for Apple’s education discount, you must fall under one of the following groups:

  • A current or newly admitted student at a higher education institution (college or university)
  • A parent purchasing on behalf of a child who is a higher education student
  • A faculty or staff member at any K–12 or higher education institution
  • A home educator (such as a homeschooling parent)

K–12 students themselves aren’t eligible, but teachers, school staff, and homeschool educators are.

How Apple Verifies Eligibility (By Region)

Depending on your country, Apple verifies your eligibility in different ways. In the United Kingdom, you’ll need to verify through UNiDAYS using your student email and school details. In the U.S., UNiDAYS isn’t always required—you can shop directly, but Apple may still ask for a student ID, acceptance letter, or school email. In Canada, Australia, and India, no upfront login is required. However, Apple may follow up with a request for proof before or after you place the order.

No matter where you are, Apple can cancel your order or charge full price if you can’t prove eligibility. So it’s best to have your documents ready just in case.

Apple Education Store Purchase Limits

Yes, Apple does place yearly purchase limits for those using educational pricing to prevent misuse. If you’re eligible, here’s what you’re allowed to buy each calendar year:

  • 1 Mac desktop (includes iMac, Mac Studio, Mac Pro, or Mac mini)
  • 1 Mac laptop (includes MacBook Air or MacBook Pro)
  • 2 iPads (any model from the iPad Air or iPad Pro line)
  • 2 accessories (these must be items offered with education pricing, like Magic Keyboard, Magic Trackpad, Apple Pencil, etc.)

These limits apply per customer, per year. That means if you’re a student or faculty member, you can only buy one discounted MacBook and two iPads per year—even if you need to replace or upgrade more than one. You cannot use the education store to purchase items in bulk or on behalf of others who aren’t eligible.

Also, purchases must be for personal use. Apple prohibits reselling devices purchased through the Education Store. If Apple finds any violation or suspects misuse (like multiple orders under one name), they can cancel the order or charge the difference in price.

These limits are consistent across most countries and are stated in Apple’s official sales policies for the Education Store. So it’s best to plan your purchases accordingly.

How to Get the Student Discount

If you’re a student, parent, or educator, here’s how you can grab Apple’s education pricing. The process is nearly the same across countries, with a few small variations.

First, here are direct links to Apple’s Education Stores based on country:

  • United States
  • United Kingdom
  • Canada
  • Australia
  • India
  • Germany
  • France
  • Japan
  1. Go to your country’s Apple Education Store using the link above.
  2. Browse the eligible Mac and iPad models—student prices are listed directly on the page.
  3. Select your preferred device and customize options like storage, color, and keyboard.
  4. Add it to your cart and proceed to checkout.
  5. Apple may request proof of eligibility, like a student ID, school-issued email, or acceptance letter. It’s not always immediate, but having those ready just in case is a good idea.

In the US, Canada, Australia, India, and most countries, you can shop directly without logging in upfront. But Apple might verify eligibility before or after purchase. In the U.K., you’ll need to sign in with UNiDAYS using your university email before seeing student pricing.

Simply follow the process based on your country, and you’ll get access to Apple’s discounted pricing with minimal hassle.

Also Read:

  • How to add your student ID to Apple Wallet on iPhone

Apple’s Back to School Offer

Every year, Apple also runs a limited-time Back to School promotion in select countries. It offers extra value on top of regular student discounts, making it one of the best times to buy a Mac or iPad for school, college, or teaching.

The promotion runs on the following schedule:

  • June to September – U.S., India, and Canada
  • July to October – U.K. and most of Europe
  • January to March – Australia, New Zealand, Brazil, and South Korea

If you buy a qualifying Mac or iPad during this period, you’ll get to choose one free or discounted accessory. What you get depends on the product you purchase:

Customers must manually select the accessory at checkout. If they choose to upgrade to a more expensive option, they’ll pay the price difference.

This offer is only valid online via the Apple Education Store, in retail stores, or through 1-800-MY-APPLE. Refurbished, open-box, or reseller purchases aren’t eligible.

Bonus: Apple Music Student Plan

Students can also get 50% off the Apple Music plan, paying just $5.99/month instead of the regular $10.99. On top of that, Apple throws in free Apple TV+ for as long as you remain a verified student. The discount is valid for up to 48 months, which is enough to cover most college programs.

To activate the offer, you’ll need to verify your student status using a platform like UNiDAYS. This student deal is available in most countries where Apple Music is supported, including the U.S., U.K., Canada, Australia, and India.

Final Tip

Even if you don’t qualify, check Apple’s Refurbished Store or other retailers for deals. However, if you’re a student or educator, Apple’s Education Store is the most reliable way to save—and it only takes a few steps to verify your eligibility.

acceptedAnswer.text: Store attendants in the Apple Retail Store, third-party vendors, or Authorized Campus Resellers may ask you to provide proof of eligibility (for example, the current semester’s tuition fee receipt or your current school ID). title.rendered: Apple is Looking Into Buying Perplexity AI — Its Biggest-ever Acquisition

content.rendered:
Apple might be cooking up its biggest AI move yet. According to a report from Bloomberg, Apple executives have recently discussed the possibility of acquiring Perplexity AI—a rising startup known for its AI-powered search engine and chatbot that works like a smart assistant. While no formal offer has been made, these early internal talks hint at a major shift in Apple’s AI strategy. And it goes far beyond just making Siri smarter.

Apple Is in Early Talks

Adrian Perica, Apple’s head of mergers and acquisitions, is said to have discussed the idea with Eddy Cue and other top decision-makers behind Apple’s AI efforts. They’ve reportedly held multiple meetings with Perplexity over the past few months. One option on the table is a partnership. But another, much bigger possibility? A full acquisition.

Why Apple Is Interested in Perplexity AI

Why now? Because Apple is behind. While companies like Google and Meta are racing ahead with advanced AI tools and large language models, Apple has taken a slower, more cautious approach. Even at WWDC 2025, Apple didn’t unveil anything revolutionary. The big Siri upgrade, once promised as part of Apple Intelligence, is now delayed until 2026.

That’s where Perplexity could come in. The startup has developed a powerful AI search experience that seamlessly blends real-time web results with conversational answers, much like a combination of ChatGPT and Google. It has already gained about 15 million monthly users, and it works across multiple platforms. Apple has reportedly been impressed, with Cue even confirming under oath during the Google antitrust trial that Apple had discussions with Perplexity.

What’s In It for Apple?

So what does Apple want from this deal?

  • An AI-powered search engine: Apple has long relied on Google as the default search on iPhones and Macs. That deal brings in around $20 billion a year, but it’s now under threat from antitrust regulators. If Apple loses that agreement, Perplexity could be a strong fallback.
  • Better AI talent: Perplexity has a strong engineering team and proven tech. Buying the company wouldn’t just give Apple software—it would bring in top talent too.
  • A smarter Siri: Apple has been struggling to catch up in the assistant space. Integrating Perplexity’s conversational AI could give Siri a much-needed boost, especially now that Apple Intelligence features are lagging.

There’s also a hiring battle happening behind the scenes. Apple and Meta are both trying to hire top AI minds like Daniel Gross, co-founder of Safe Superintelligence Inc. (Gross previously sold a startup named Cue to Apple and helped shape early versions of Siri). Meta even attempted to acquire Perplexity earlier this year, but failed, instead investing $14.3 billion in Scale AI.

If Apple goes ahead with the deal, it would be its biggest acquisition ever. Perplexity is now valued at around $14 billion—nearly five times the amount Apple paid for Beats in 2014. Apple hasn’t spent that kind of money on a single deal before.

What Happens Next?

Of course, nothing is certain yet. These are still internal discussions. Apple hasn’t made a formal offer, and Perplexity says it’s not aware of any active M&A talks. There’s also a possible complication: Samsung, Apple’s biggest smartphone rival, is reportedly working on its own partnership with Perplexity.

Still, if Apple is serious about catching up in AI, this may be its moment. Perplexity brings search tech, talent, and a real product already used by millions. And with the clock ticking on its Google deal, Apple might not want to wait much longer.

title.rendered: iPhone 20 Will Be Fully All-Screen by 2027, in Two Stages

content.rendered:
The iPhone has come a long way from its thick-bezel, Home Button days. But even in 2025, there’s still one thing Apple hasn’t pulled off: a true all-screen iPhone. No notch. No Dynamic Island. No punch hole. Just pure display from edge to edge. Now, reports say Apple is finally getting there — but not all at once. It’s happening in two big steps, starting next year and finishing with a major redesign in 2027.

Step One: Shrinking the Dynamic Island

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman and other credible leakers, Apple has a roadmap. And it starts with shrinking the Dynamic Island in the iPhone 17. Not removing it entirely, just making it smaller. The real breakthrough will come the following year with the iPhone 18 Pro, which is expected to hide the Face ID sensors under the screen. This will leave just the front camera visible as a small hole — no more pill-shaped cutout.

Step Two: The True All-Screen iPhone in 2027

But that’s not the end goal. The real transformation comes in 2027, when Apple celebrates the iPhone’s 20th anniversary. That’s when we’re expected to see the first iPhone with both the Face ID system and the selfie camera completely hidden under the display. No holes, no cutouts, just screen. Gurman calls this the most ambitious design shift since the original iPhone was introduced.

What the iPhone 20 Might Look Like

Here’s what else is being said about the iPhone 20:

  • It could have a curved, almost wraparound design made of a single piece of glass. Apple reportedly refers to it as a “monolithic” look.
  • The front, sides, and back may all flow together as one seamless surface.
  • Apple might be using something called “secondary-formed glass” to pull this off, making the device feel like it’s carved from one solid block.
  • The design isn’t just about looks — it also helps support Apple’s all-screen ambitions and ties into its 2030 carbon-neutral goals.
  • Internally, the company may also be combining components to reduce parts and increase manufacturing efficiency.

It won’t be easy, though. A monolithic glass iPhone is expensive to produce, and companies usually reserve these kinds of designs for concept devices or anniversaries. Apple is known to play the long game, and the iPhone 20 might be one of those rare moments where the company goes all-in on design innovation.

iOS 26 Might Be a Sneak Peek

All of these line up with Apple’s recent iOS 26 update, which introduced a new visual theme called Liquid Glass. Many believe this is a hint at what’s coming in the hardware.

For now, Apple’s new Liquid Glass design aligns with the leaked iPhone 20 design and works in tandem.

Apple’s 2027 Vision: More Than Just iPhones

And that’s not all. 2027 could be one of Apple’s biggest years ever. Alongside the iPhone 20, Apple is reportedly working on:

  • It’s the first foldable iPhone
  • Smart glasses to rival Meta’s Ray-Ban lineup
  • A smarter Siri, powered by its own large language models
  • Even a home robot assistant that can interact using personality-driven AI

For now, the path is clear. First, iPhone 17 trims down the Dynamic Island. Then, iPhone 18 Pro hides Face ID. And finally, in 2027, the iPhone 20 removes every cutout and turns into a smooth sheet of glass. If Apple pulls this off, it might be the cleanest, most futuristic phone we’ve ever seen.

And after two decades of evolution, maybe that’s exactly what the iPhone needs.

excerpt.rendered: Apple’s two-step plan to launch a truly all-screen iPhone kicks off with iPhone 17 and culminates with the futuristic iPhone 20 in 2027. Here’s what’s coming.

title.rendered: How to use Stage Manager on iPad and Mac

content.rendered:
Your iPad or Mac can turn into a better multitasking device with Stage Manager, a multitasking feature that offers a more intuitive environment to work with multiple apps at once. If you are unaware of Stage Manager, read on, and I will walk you through everything you need to know about the feature, including how to use it on your iPad and Mac.

Table of Contents
  • What is Stage Manager?
  • Which iPads and Macs support Stage Manager?
  • How to turn on and off Stage Manager
    • Turn on Stage Manager on iPad
    • Turn on Stage Manager on Mac
  • How to use Stage Manager on iPad
    • Group apps together for specific tasks or projects
    • Switch between apps
    • Switch to full screen or exit from the group
  • How to use Stage Manager on Mac
    • Group apps together for specific tasks or projects
    • Switch between apps
  • Is Stage Manager better than using traditional multitasking methods?

What is Stage Manager?

When you attend a concert, you can notice how optimally managed the stage looks. From the lighting, sound, and design to adeptly timing performances from your favorite artists, it’s all perfectly handled by the stage manager working behind the scenes.

Likewise, you have Stage Manager on your iPad and Mac to perfectly manage your stage, i.e., your screen. With Stage Manager, you can seamlessly switch between apps, group apps for a specific task, arrange and resize the app windows, and more on your iPad and Mac that support it.

Which iPads and Macs support Stage Manager?

Unfortunately, Stage Manager is not supported on all iPad and Mac models. Check to see if your device is included in the list below.

Stage Manager-supported iPads running iPadOS 26:

  • 13-inch iPad Pro (M4 chip)
  • 12.9-inch iPad Pro (3rd generation and later)
  • 11-inch iPad Pro (1st generation and later)
  • iPad Air (3rd generation and later)
  • iPad mini (5th generation and later)
  • iPad (8th generation and later)

For those of you who didn’t find your iPad in the above list, don’t worry—you can still multitask; check out our iPad multitasking guide to learn how.

Stage Manager supported Macs:

  • All the Macs running macOS Ventura and later support Stage Manager

How to turn on and off Stage Manager

To start using Stage Manager, you first need to turn it on. Here is how to do it on your iPad and Mac.

Turn on Stage Manager on iPad

You can turn on Stage Manager on your iPad like this:

  1. Go to Settings > Multitasking & Gestures.
  2. Select Stage Manager in the menu above.

  3. Alternatively, open Control Centre and tap the Stage Manager icon to turn it on.

That’s it. You are now ready to start using Stage Manager on your iPad.

When you want to turn off Stage Manager, repeat the same steps.

Turn on Stage Manager on Mac

Just like on an iPad, you can turn on Stage Manager on a Mac from the System Settings app as well as the Control Center. Follow the steps:

  1. Head to System Settings → Display & Dock.
  2. Toggle on the Stage Manager option.

  3. Alternatively, you can turn on Stage Manager from the Control Center, too, just like on an iPad. Access the Control Center and click the Stage Manager icon.

Repeat the same steps when you want to turn off Stage Manager on your Mac.

Unlike on an iPad, you can customize certain behavior of apps in Stage Manager on a Mac. This includes choosing whether recent apps appear in Stage Manager and how the app windows appear when you are using the feature.

To do this, head to System Settings > Desktop & Dock, and you will see a couple of options in the Stage Manager section. Modify these options according to your preference.

How to use Stage Manager on iPad

Using Stage Manager on an iPad is easy. Below, I have listed everything you can do with Stage Manager on your iPad.

Group apps together for specific tasks or projects

You can group up to four apps that stack on top of each other. Here is how to do it:

  1. Open an app and tap the three dots at the top-center of the screen.
  2. Tap Add Another Window.

  3. Select the other app you want to group with.

  4. Now, both your apps will be grouped. Likewise, you can group up to four apps. Alternatively, you can drag an app from the Recent app stack on the left side of your screen or the Dock and drop it on top of an already open app to group it.

  5. To resize the grouped apps, drag from the corner handles on the app window and resize it into your preferred size.

Switch between apps

To switch between apps or grouped apps, simply tap on the desired app either in the Recent app stack on the left hand of your screen or in the Dock at the bottom.

Switch to full screen or exit from the group

If you want the app to switch to full screen, just tap on the three dots in the middle of the app screen and then tap Enter Full Screen.

Likewise, if you want to minimize or close an app, tap Minimize or Close.

How to use Stage Manager on Mac

Using Stage Manager on your Mac is slightly different than using it on an iPad. Here is how to use it effectively.

Group apps together for specific tasks or projects

To group apps with Stage Manager on a Mac, drag an app from the Recent app stack on the left side of your screen and drop it on top of the already-open app. This will group both apps. You can add up to four apps to the group.

You can resize the app window by simply dragging it from any of the four corners or even sides.

Switch between apps

When you want to switch between apps in the same group, just click on the app; even if a tiny part of it is visible on the display, click it.

To switch to a different app that is not part of the group, click on the app’s thumbnail you want to switch to in the Recent app stack on the left side of your screen.

Is Stage Manager better than using traditional multitasking methods?

There is no way of saying one is better than the other, as it all depends on your preference. You can try out both traditional multitasking methods and Stage Manager and choose whichever makes you comfortable and allows you to complete your tasks speedily.

Signing off…

Stage Manager provides an alternative way to multitask on your iPad and Mac. If traditional multitasking methods do not suit your workflow, give Stage Manager a try and see if it meets your needs.

FAQs

Can I use Stage Manager with an external monitor on my iPad?

Yes, you can, but only on these supported iPads, i.e iPad Air (5th generation), iPad Air 11-inch (M2), iPad Air 13-inch (M2), iPad Pro 11-inch (3rd generation and later), iPad Pro 11-inch (M4), iPad Pro 12.9-inch (5th generation and later), iPad Pro 13-inch (M4).

Can Stage Manager be used with multiple desktops on a Mac?

Yes, you can use Stage Manager with multiple desktops.

  • How to use Mission Control on Mac
  • How to switch between users on Mac

acceptedAnswer.text: Store attendants in the Apple Retail Store, third-party vendors, or Authorized Campus Resellers may ask you to provide proof of eligibility (for example, the current semester’s tuition fee receipt or your current school ID). title.rendered: Official iPhone 16e Wallpapers in 4K – Download Now

content.rendered:
Apple introduced a new addition to its iPhone 16 family with the launch of the iPhone 16e, bringing an exciting set of iPhone 16e stock wallpapers. Whether you own an iPhone 16e or another iPhone model, these high-resolution 4K wallpapers will give your device a sleek and modern look.

iPhone 16e Wallpaper Collection

Apple has opted for a silver and black theme for the primary wallpaper design, exuding a futuristic aesthetic that perfectly complements the iPhone 16e. Alongside this, stunning ultramarine wallpaper and other vibrant color options are available, making it easy to match your home and lock screen to your style.

ADZ Wallpapers (@aravdz) shared these wallpapers, which maintain Apple’s signature minimalistic look while offering a refreshed visual appeal. The collection includes both dark and light variants, ensuring compatibility with your iPhone’s Dark Mode settings for a seamless experience.

Download iPhone 16e wallpapers in 4K

If you’re looking to download iPhone 16e wallpapers in 4K resolution, you’re in the right place. These wallpapers are optimized for Apple’s OLED and Super Retina XDR displays, delivering deep blacks, vibrant colors, and sharp details.

  • Compatibility: Works on all iPhones, including iPhone 15, iPhone 14, and older models
  • Resolution: 4K (Ultra HD)
  • Formats: PNG & JPEG

How to Download and Set Up iPhone 16e Wallpapers

Click the download link below each wallpaper. If the image opens in full-screen mode, tap and hold it, then select “Save to Photos” to store it in your gallery.

  • Open Settings → Tap Wallpaper → Select Add New Wallpaper.
  • Choose the downloaded image from your photo library.
  • Adjust the positioning if needed, then tap Set as Lock Screen, Home Screen, or Both.

That’s it! Your iPhone now has a fresh new look.

Why Choose iPhone 16e Stock Wallpapers?

  • Free to download: No hidden costs, just stunning visuals.
  • Apple-optimized design: Matches the aesthetic of the new iPhone 16e.
  • High-resolution 4K quality: Perfect for Super Retina XDR displays.
  • Light & dark mode compatibility: Adapts to your theme preference.

iPhone 16e Wallpaper Has a Hidden Meaning

Apple never misses a chance to sneak in some clever design details, and the iPhone 16e wallpaper is no exception. At first glance, it might just look like a sleek, reflective sphere—but there’s actually a hidden meaning behind it.

According to John Gruber of Daring Fireball, Apple’s default wallpapers for the iPhone 16 lineup subtly hint at the number of rear cameras each model has. The iPhone 16e, with its single-lens camera, features a lone sphere. Meanwhile, the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro wallpapers showcase two and three elements, respectively—mirroring their dual- and triple-camera setups.

It’s a small detail, but one that shows Apple’s signature attention to design. Clever, right?

Final Thoughts

These new iPhone 16e wallpapers will breathe new life into your iPhone’s display. Whether you’re rocking an iPhone 16e or an older iPhone, these 4K stock wallpapers ensure a visually immersive experience.

If you’re considering an upgrade, the iPhone 16e is an excellent entry-level option that shares many features with the standard iPhone 16 while keeping costs lower. Explore more stunning wallpapers from this talented artist on X: @privatetalky. Huge thanks to them!

Check out our iPhone 16e vs. iPhone 16 comparison article to learn more and choose the right one for you.

title.rendered: 10+ New Safari Features in iOS 26 and macOS Tahoe You Probably Missed

content.rendered:
Apple’s Safari browser has received a substantial upgrade with the release of iOS 26 and macOS 26 Tahoe, as revealed at WWDC 2025. These updates bring a modern Liquid Glass design, faster performance, enhanced privacy, and a host of new features that make Safari more powerful and user-friendly across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Here’s a deep dive into everything new in Safari—and how it transforms your web experience.

A Gorgeous New Look with Liquid Glass Design

Apple’s Liquid Glass aesthetic now spans across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe, and Safari fully embraces it.

1. Translucent Interface Elements

The address bar, toolbars, and tabs in Safari now have a glassy, translucent appearance. The refractive controls feel like liquid glass layered over your content.  

On iOS 26, the address bar blends seamlessly with the webpage you’re viewing. Moreover, the content appears from the top edge to the bottom of the screen. So, you can see more of the page than the previous white blocks.

 

On macOS Tahoe, the address bar and toolbar at the top of the browser reflect colors from the webpage. Therefore, as you scroll through the page, the colors change, making the interface feel more dynamic and immersive. This transparency makes your content stand out. 

2. Compact Layout Style That Prioritizes Content

Along with the new design, Safari in iOS 26 offers three different placement options for the address bar: 

  • Compact (default)
  • Bottom
  • Top

The Compact layout hides the share, bookmark, and tab settings behind the three-dot button on the left of the URL bar. However, the Bottom and Top options retain the address bar’s position from earlier iOS versions, with a translucent look. Here’s how it looks:

 

You can switch between these layouts by going to Settings > Apps > Safari and selecting a layout under the Tab section, giving you flexibility to choose what you like.

Whichever layout you select, when you scroll through a webpage, the URL bar and buttons collapse into a single, narrow bar that just displays the webpage address. So, you can have an edge‑to‑edge browsing experience with more content on the screen. 

3. Minimal Buttons and Smarter Interactions

Safari in iOS 26 adopts a minimalist toolbar:

  • Only a back button appears beside the address bar.
  • Tap and hold the back button to reveal your browsing history or access the forward button.
  • Tap and hold the address bar for quick tab options like Close Tab, Switch Tab Group, and more.

You are now able to tap and hold the address bar in order to show the tab settings like Close Tab, Close Other Tabs, Switch Tab Groups, etc. 

4. Rounded Tabs and Revamped Sidebar on Mac

On macOS Tahoe:

  • Tabs now float as rounded, separated elements—improving visibility and navigation.
  • A redesigned sidebar includes iCloud Tabs, Saved, and Shared With, making your content easier to find and organize. 

5. Unified and Customizable Safari App Icons

Safari’s app icon now follows the Liquid Glass look. You can choose from:

  • Light
  • Dark
  • Tinted
  • New Clear (glassy) version

This aligns Safari’s aesthetic with other redesigned system icons.

6. Web Apps for All Websites  

Safari 26 revolutionizes web apps by making it possible to add any website to your Home Screen as a web app on iOS 26, even if the site wasn’t built as a Progressive Web App (PWA).  

This helps users who desire direct access to their favorite sites without getting their browser cluttered with tabs or bookmarks. Here’s how it works:  

  • If you add a site to your Home Screen (through the Share menu in Safari), it opens as a stand-alone web app by default. That is, it comes up as a full-screen app without Safari’s characteristic browser interface, which makes it look and feel very much like a native app.  
  • You can choose whether a website opens as a web app or within Safari when adding it to the Home Screen. In the Share menu, toggle on/off Open as Web App. If disabled, the site will open in a new Safari tab, preserving the traditional browsing experience.  

  • Web apps in Safari now offer push notifications (if the site allows it) to keep you informed without opening the browser. You can also access offline reading (for sites with PWA support) and smoother animations due to the Liquid Glass design.  
  • macOS Tahoe also supports web apps. Tap the Share button on the toolbar and choose Add to Dock > Add. It will add the website to the Dock for easy access. These web apps launch in their own window, independently of Safari, and have the same simplified, app-like experience as on iOS 26.  

Privacy and Security Upgrades

Privacy is a cornerstone of Safari, and iOS 26 and macOS Tahoe introduce key upgrades to protect your data.

7. Improved Anti-Fingerprinting and Link Tracking Protection

Safari 26 has enhanced its defenses against fingerprinting, a technique employed by some websites to track users across the internet by analyzing their device’s unique characteristics. This ensures your browsing habits remain private. 

Before iOS 26, this auto-removal of tracking parameters from URL feature was only enabled for Private Browsing on Safari. But now, it’s set for all browsing by default, giving you peace of mind while browsing. 

Visual and Multimedia Enhancements

To make the Liquid Glass design more dynamic, Apple has introduced several visual enhancements. 

8. HDR Photo Support in Websites

Safari now supports HDR images, making photos on websites more vibrant with higher contrast and color accuracy, especially when viewed on HDR-capable devices.

9. SVG Icon Support

Apple also included SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) icons across the Safari browser, including the Start page, Favorites, and Favicons.

This makes icons sharper, more visually appealing, and more scalable, improving their appearance at any size without pixelation.  

Performance Boosts and Battery Gains

Safari is faster and more efficient than ever, thanks to optimizations on iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe.  

10. Up to 50% Faster Page Loading

Apple claims Safari 26:

  • Loads frequently visited sites up to 50% faster than Chrome, Edge, and Firefox
  • Achieved through benchmarks like JetStream 2.2, MotionMark 1.3.1, and Speedometer 3.1

Devices tested include:

  • iPhone 16 Pro Max (iOS 26)
  • MacBook Air with M4 chip (macOS Tahoe)

11. Longer Streaming Time on Mac

Safari in macOS Tahoe offers:

  • Up to 4 extra hours of video playback vs Chrome
  • Tested with 1080p content on a MacBook Air with Apple Silicon

This makes Safari more battery-efficient for streaming and media consumption.

Tools for Developers

Safari 26 includes major upgrades for developers:

  • WebGPU Support: Safari now officially supports WebGPU, a feature that enables websites to access your device’s graphics power for enhanced visuals, such as 3D video games or animations. This paves the way for more immersive web experiences. 
  • CSS and WebKit Enhancements: New features in CSS include improved anchor positioning for tooltips, enhanced scroll animations, and refined text-wrap capabilities, all of which contribute to cleaner and more polished web content. 
  • SwiftUI WebView and Web Apps: SwiftUI can now be utilized by developers to embed web content into apps with greater ease, and Safari allows for web apps on iOS 26. This implies that you can now open web app links directly, simplifying your workflow. 

What’s Still Missing

There is clear progress, yet a few pieces are still not here:

  • No Vertical Tabs: Many users were disappointed that the update does not include vertical tabs, a feature available in browsers like Edge and Firefox. Vertical tabs could save screen space, especially on smaller MacBook displays, but Apple has not implemented this yet. 
  • Mail App Enhancements: Some users expected improvements to Safari integration with the Mail app, like better handling of multiple email addresses or easier attachment management. These upgrades have not been announced, and a future update may tackle them.
  • Mixed Feelings on Liquid Glass: The Liquid Glass look is striking, yet some users find it distracting or harder to read, especially with the transparent toolbar on macOS. Others have toned the effect down but still want the compact tab layout back.

Apple will likely refine Safari based on real-world feedback, so some of these gaps may close in upcoming updates.

Safari Has Leveled Up—Here’s What It Means for You

Safari in iOS 26 and macOS 26 Tahoe blends modern visuals with real-world usability and developer-focused enhancements. Whether you’re streaming, reading, or building web experiences, this is Safari’s biggest leap in years.

Which Safari 26 feature is your favorite? Drop your thoughts in the comments.

title.rendered: 7 Genius Things You Can Do with Apple Intelligence in the Shortcuts App

content.rendered:
Apple Intelligence didn’t steal the spotlight this year, but one thing quietly changed the game: it now works inside the Shortcuts app.

That means you can automate tasks using AI. No need to repeat the same actions every day. Just build a Shortcut once, and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest with a single tap.

Not sure what to use it for? Here are 7 practical things you can now do with Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts, things that weren’t possible before.

Note These Shortcuts require iOS 26, iPadOS 26, or macOS 26 Tahoe, and they work seamlessly across all three platforms. You can also add them to your Share Sheet or automations to make your workflow even easier.

1. Turn Voice Memos into Summaries and Save Them to Notes

Got a long voice recording? Whether it’s a meeting, a random idea, or a voice memo to yourself, you can now create a Shortcut that:

  • Transcribes the audio
  • Summarizes the content
  • Saves both to the Notes app

It works offline (on-device), supports up to 10 minutes of audio, and saves you from reading full transcripts.

Get this Shortcut

2. Summarize Any PDF with One Tap – No Copying Needed

There’s currently no direct way to upload a PDF to Apple Intelligence and get a summary. You’d usually have to copy the entire text manually and paste it into a writing tool with a Summarize option. But now, you can simplify this process with a Shortcut. 

Open a PDF in Safari, Mail, or the Files app, tap Share, and choose your Shortcut. Apple Intelligence will read the entire PDF and give you a quick summary. You can even tweak the tone by making it formal, friendly, or turning it into a list. 

Get this Shortcut

3. Get a Morning Briefing with Weather, Calendar, and Reminders

Imagine starting your day with a Shortcut that pulls today’s calendar events, reminders, and weather, and then asks Apple Intelligence to write it all out like a personal morning briefing. The result? A natural-language summary of your day, created in seconds. 

Set it to run at a specific time every morning, and you’re good to go.

Get this Shortcut

4. Summarize Emails the Way You Like

The Mail app does have a summary feature, but it often skips important details, sounds too formal, or doesn’t highlight key info clearly. With Shortcuts, you’re in control. Just:

  • Print the email to PDF
  • Share it with your custom Shortcut
  • Let Apple Intelligence summarize it using your own prompt

You decide what the summary sounds like, whether it’s casual, concise, detailed, or anything in between.

Get this Shortcut

5. Turn Podcasts into Actionable Notes

If you don’t always have time to finish an episode. This Shortcut can:

  • Fetches the latest episode from an RSS feed
  • Transcribes the audio
  • Summarizes key takeaways
  • Saves it to Notes

Perfect for staying updated without going through the hassle of summarizing the podcast every day. 

Get this Shortcut

6. Clean Up Random Thoughts into Organized Notes

You’re thinking out loud, or maybe rambling an idea into your mic, not a problem. This Shortcut takes what you say and turns it into a structured, bulleted list. It separates tasks, dates, or ideas, and also saves the full transcript for later use. Great for messy minds.

Get this Shortcut

7. Build Your Own Chatbot with Follow-Up Support

Apple says they are not interested in creating an Apple Intelligence chatbot. However, you can easily do that yourself with the “Use Model” action.

You can:

  • Write custom prompts
  • Ask Apple Intelligence or ChatGPT anything
  • Turn on “Follow Up” to keep the conversation going

You can build a chatbot for planning, journaling, decision-making, or even just chatting for fun. And unlike Siri, the AI doesn’t just forward you to ChatGPT, it answers in your chosen style and context, based on your input and how your Shortcut is built.

Get this Shortcut

Want more Shortcuts and Apple Intelligence tips? Check out our full guide to Spotlight in macOS 26 and supercharge your productivity even further.

What’s Next for Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts?

Right now, Apple Intelligence only works with text and audio in Shortcuts. But Apple says it’s just the beginning. Soon, it’ll be able to understand your calendar, reminders, Clock app, and more. That means even smarter automations, such as knowing when you’re free, reminding you to leave, or adjusting based on your daily routine.

Apple Intelligence is smart on its own, but inside Shortcuts, it becomes yours. You’re not just asking it questions. You’re turning it into your personal assistant, built around how you live.

title.rendered: Spotlight in macOS 26 Tahoe: Everything You Can Do With It

content.rendered:
Spotlight has always been a quick way to find things on your Mac. With macOS 26 (Tahoe), Spotlight is no longer just a search tool. It’s now your all-in-one command center that helps you get things done faster, smarter, and without switching apps all the time.

Here’s everything that’s new, what you can do with it, and why Spotlight in macOS 26 Tahoe might become your favorite Mac feature.

Table of Contents
  • Browse, Not Just Search
  • Find iPhone Apps from Your Mac
  • Run Actions Without Opening Any App
  • It Works Inside Apps Too
  • Smarter Shortcuts + Apple Intelligence
  • Quick Keys to Save Time
  • Clipboard History Is Finally Built In

    1. Browse, Not Just Search

    If you don’t remember the exact name of the app or file you’re searching for, no problem. Spotlight in macOS 26 now has a browse mode that shows everything in a single, scrollable interface.

    After opening Spotlight, press Command (⌘) + 1 or click the Apps icon to browse your apps. Press Command (⌘) + 2 or click the Files icon to browse files. You can also filter by file types like PDFs or JPEGs. It even pulls documents from iCloud.

    At the top of browse mode, Spotlight also offers suggestions based on your routine, current activity, and even the time of day. For example, if you typically send a report to your manager on Fridays, Spotlight will automatically surface that file and the contact.

    2. Find iPhone Apps from Your Mac

    Thanks to iPhone Mirroring, Spotlight can now find and suggest apps installed on your iPhone. So if you need something from your phone while you’re at your desk, you don’t have to get up or switch devices.

    Just search in Spotlight on your Mac, and when you select the iPhone app. It will open directly inside the iPhone Mirroring app on your Mac. Ensure both devices have Wi-Fi and Bluetooth enabled, are signed in with the same Apple ID, and are positioned close to each other. 

    3. Run Actions Without Opening Any App

    Spotlight is no longer just about finding apps and files—you can now perform hundreds of tasks instantly, without opening any app. Simply type a command and press Return. For instance, typing “start timer,” entering the duration, and pressing Return will start the timer in the Clock app, all without needing to launch it.

    Here are just a few things Spotlight can now handle directly:

    • Send an email or message to someone
    • Create a new calendar event
    • Record a voice note or create a new note
    • Set a reminder
    • Start a FaceTime call
    • Play a podcast
    • Move, rename, or delete files
    • Eject external drives
    • Get directions in Apple Maps
    • Run custom Shortcuts
    • Generate AI images or text summaries via Apple Intelligence

    These are just examples—Spotlight can handle system-level actions, app-specific tasks, and personalized workflows—and support will keep growing as more apps integrate with it. 

    However, as of now, Spotlight cannot directly change system settings, such as adjusting brightness, toggling Wi-Fi, or enabling features. You can still use it to launch specific sections of the System Settings app, where you can make those adjustments manually. 

    4. It Works Inside Apps Too

    If you’re editing a photo and can’t remember where the tone adjustment tool is. Just open Spotlight and type “adjust tone.” If the app supports it, Spotlight will take you straight there. You can even search the menu bar commands.

    Here’s the best part—Spotlight is getting smarter as more apps get on board. Apple now lets developers plug their app features into Spotlight using something called App Intents. That means you’ll soon be able to do things like send files, apply filters, or start meetings from Spotlight using third-party apps too.

    5. Smarter Shortcuts + Apple Intelligence

    Spotlight is now tightly integrated with Shortcuts. Since Shortcuts now support intelligent actions using Apple Intelligence, you can trigger these smart Shortcuts directly from Spotlight.

    For example, you can create a Shortcut that collects text from an open webpage, uses Apple Intelligence to summarize it, and then returns the summary instantly. You can also translate selected text and paste it back automatically.

    Other useful Shortcuts you might consider:

    • Resize or convert an image with one command
    • Turn any web article into a PDF
    • Create a task in your to-do app based on the copied text
    • Schedule a quick meeting with pre-filled details

    Spotlight also learns which Shortcuts you use frequently and suggests them based on your current activity.

    6. Quick Keys to Save Time

    Yes, you can now run actions and even custom shortcuts directly from Spotlight. But you can make it even faster by assigning custom quick keys to your most-used actions.

    For example, if you frequently add reminders, you can assign ‘ar’ as a quick key. Then, whenever you type ‘ar’ in Spotlight, it will instantly suggest adding a reminder. Similarly, you can:

    • Type sm to send a message
    • Type st to start a timer
    • Type se to send an email

    You can also customize these, so your most frequent actions are just two letters away.

    7. Clipboard History Is Finally Built In

    Until now, macOS didn’t have a built-in clipboard history—you could only copy one item at a time or rely on third-party apps. That changes with this Spotlight update. macOS 26 introduces a native clipboard history built right into Spotlight.

    Just open Spotlight and press Command (⌘) + 4, or click the clipboard icon to view your clipboard history. It’s easy to access and works with everything: text, images, web links, and even files from Finder. You can also delete individual copied items or clear the entire history. Just copy multiple items, access the history, and paste whatever you want.

    Spotlight Can Now Finally Replace Alfred or Raycast

    This year, Liquid Glass has taken over the internet as the headline feature. However, if you’re an advanced macOS user or rely on tools like Raycast or Alfred, Spotlight might be the real highlight of macOS 26. It’s faster, smarter, more capable—and genuinely more helpful in day-to-day work.

    It replaces many third-party features, including clipboard history, file search, quick actions, and in-app control execution.

    And maybe, just maybe this is the foundation for the smarter Siri Apple has been promising.

title.rendered: How to Transfer Your Data from a Windows PC to a Mac

content.rendered:
Switching from a Windows PC to a Mac is exciting—but transferring your files, photos, documents, music, and apps can feel overwhelming. The good news? There are several reliable methods for transferring your data safely and easily. In this guide, I’ll walk you through six proven methods to transfer data from a Windows PC to a Mac using built-in tools, cloud services, or external drives.

Table of Contents
  • Preparations Before Transferring Data from Windows to Mac
  • 6 Ways to Transfer Data from Windows to Mac
    • 1. Use Apple Migration Assistant
      • What Transfers:
      • Tips for Migration Assistant
    • 2. Transfer via Windows File Sharing
      • What Transfers:
      • Tips
    • 3. Using Cloud Storage (iCloud, Google Drive, etc.)
      • Tips
    • 4. Using External Storage (USB or Hard Drive)
      • Tips
    • 5. Network-Attached Storage (NAS)
      • Tips
    • 6. Use Third-Party Tools
      • Tips
  • Post-Transfer Checklist
  • Troubleshooting: Can't Transfer Data to Mac?
  • Transfer Files to Mac Without the Stress

Preparations Before Transferring Data from Windows to Mac

Start strong with these essential pre-transfer steps to avoid data loss or confusion:

  1. Update Your Devices: Ensure your Windows PC runs the latest version of Windows 11 (Settings > Windows Update) and your Mac is updated to the latest macOS (System Settings > General > Software Update).

  2. Back Up Everything: Use Windows Backup (Settings > Accounts > Windows Backup), Acronis True Image, or an external drive to create a full backup of your PC.
  3. Check Mac Storage: Make sure your Mac has enough free space for the incoming files (System Settings > General > Storage). If transferring 500GB, your Mac should have at least 500GB of free space.

  4. Organize Files: Group files into folders like Documents, Photos, and Videos. Delete unnecessary files to streamline the transfer.
  5. Check Compatibility: Some files (.exe programs) won’t run on macOS. Convert media formats like .wma to .mp3 using VLC Media Player.
  6. Make a Software List: Identify your frequently used Windows apps. Some may have Mac versions; research alternatives where needed.
  7. Note Login Credentials: Jot down Microsoft account info, email logins, and Wi-Fi passwords.
  8. Gather Equipment: You may need an external USB drive, a Thunderbolt cable, or a reliable internet/Ethernet connection.
  9. Adjust Security Settings: Disable firewall, VPN, or antivirus temporarily to ensure smooth transfers.

6 Ways to Transfer Data from Windows to Mac

Let’s explore each method with how-tos, pros, cons, and expert tips.

1. Use Apple Migration Assistant

Best For: Full profile transfers during Mac setup

Requires: Both devices are connected to the same network or Ethernet

Steps:

  1. On your Windows PC, download Migration Assistant from Apple’s official website. It’s compatible with macOS Sonoma 14.4 or later and Windows 10 or later. 
  2. Open Migration Assistant on both devices. On Mac, find it in Applications > Utilities or search via Spotlight. 
  3. Follow the on-screen prompts to connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi network or use an Ethernet cable. Ensure you are logged in as an administrator on your PC. 
  4. On the Mac, select From a Windows PC, then click Continue.

  5. Enter the code displayed on your Mac into the Windows Migration Assistant. 

  6. Now, Migration Assistant analyzes your computer’s data and determines how much storage space each type of file takes up. Scroll down and select the data you want to move.
  7. To initiate the transfer, click Continue. Wait for it to be completed (time depends on data size and connection speed).

  8. After the transfer is finished, exit Migration Assistant on both PC and Mac. To access the files, log into the migrated account on your Mac.

  9. Set up your Apple Account on your Mac to sync it or access content from Apple.

If you need to transfer data from another Windows user account, log in to that account on your PC and repeat the steps.

What Transfers:

You can choose what data you want to transfer using Migration Assistant. This includes: 

  • Email and email settings from Windows Mail and Outlook are moved to the Mail app. 
  • Contacts from People (Windows 10 or later), Outlook, and the Contacts folder in your home directory all go to the Contacts app. 
  • Appointments from Outlook and Calendar (Windows 10 or later) transfer to the Calendar app. 
  • Tasks from Outlook are saved to the Reminders app.  
  • Music, podcasts, audiobooks, and movies/TV series are accessed through the Music app, Podcasts app, Books app, and Apple TV app, respectively. 
  • Bookmarks and the homepage from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Internet Explorer, and other browsers are transferred to Safari. 
  • Custom desktop images, language preferences, known Wi-Fi networks, and location settings are automatically saved in System Settings. 
  • Documents and other things from your home directory are now in your home folder. Photos and other images are also moved to the home folder. To add them to the Photos app, you can either add them manually or open Photos and let it search and import them. 
  • Non-system files and documents from the system disk (usually the C drive) and other accessible drives go to the Shared folder.  

Pros

  • Transfers entire user profiles
  • Maintains folder structure and system settings
  • No extra software needed

Cons

  • Can be slow for large transfers
  • Apps from Windows won’t run on macOS

Tips for Migration Assistant 

  1. Use during initial Mac setup for the smoothest experience. 
  2. Plug both devices into power to avoid interruptions. 
  3. If the transfer stalls, restart both devices and try again. You must close antivirus/firewalls temporarily if the connection fails. 
  4. Ensure both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network band (e.g., 5 GHz). Use Ethernet to speed things up. 

2. Transfer via Windows File Sharing

Best For: Transferring select files over Wi-Fi or Ethernet

Mac Setup:

  1. Go to System Settings > General > Sharing

  2. Toggle on File Sharing and click the info button next to it.

  3. Next, click the Options section at the bottom.

  4. Toggle on Share files and folders using SMB.
  5. Under the Windows File Sharing section, check the box next to the account name whose files you wish to access on Windows.

  6. Enter the user’s password, then click OK.
  7. Click Done to save your choice.

     
  8. Take note of the IP address displayed under the File Sharing: On at the top of the window (e.g., smb://your-mac-address). 

Windows Setup:

  1. Launch File Explorer and right-click a folder (e.g., Documents). 
  2. Select Properties > Sharing > Share.  
  3. Add Everyone or a specific user and note the network path (e.g., \\your-pc-name\folder). 

To Transfer:

  1. Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi or Ethernet network. 
  2. On your Mac, open Finder, click Go in the menu bar, and select Connect to Server.

  3. Enter smb://<Windows_IP_address> and click Connect.

  4. Alternatively, click Network in the sidebar and locate your Windows PC. 
  5. Enter your Windows PC’s username and password if prompted. 
  6. Drag and drop files from the Windows shared folder to your Mac. 

What Transfers:

  • Any files or folders you’ve shared (e.g., Documents, Photos, Videos). 
  • Does not transfer user accounts or app settings. 

Pros

  • Fast on modern networks
  • No hardware needed
  • Great for selective file transfers

Cons

  • Setup can be complex
  • May be blocked by firewalls or antivirus software

Tips 

  • Use an Ethernet cable for faster, more stable transfers. 
  • Disable Windows Defender Firewall temporarily if the connection fails (re-enable after). 
  • Name shared folders clearly to avoid confusion. 
  • Test with a small file to ensure the connection works. 

3. Using Cloud Storage (iCloud, Google Drive, etc.)

Best For: Small-to-medium file transfers and remote access

Popular Services: 

  • iCloud: 5GB free, up to 12TB with paid plans, integrated with macOS. 
  • Google Drive: 15GB free, cross-platform, easy to use. 
  • Dropbox: 2GB free, reliable for both platforms. 
  • Microsoft OneDrive: 5GB free, great for Windows users. 

Steps to transfer files:

  1. On your Windows PC, install the cloud service app or use the browser version. 
  2. Sign in with your account (or create one). 
  3. Upload files from Windows to the cloud (e.g., drag folders to Google Drive). 
  4. On your Mac, install the same cloud service app or sign in via browser. 
  5. Download the files to your Mac or sync them via Finder. 

Pros

  • No cables needed
  • Access files from anywhere
  • Easy to share specific files or folders.

Cons

  • Limited free storage
  • Upload speed depends on the internet connection

Tips 

  1. Compress large folders (e.g., ZIP) to save space and speed up uploads. 
  2. Use a wired internet connection for faster uploads and downloads. 
  3. Enable two-factor authentication for security. 
  4. Clear cloud storage regularly to free up space. For iCloud, use selective sync to save local space. 

4. Using External Storage (USB or Hard Drive)

Best For: Large files or no internet

Steps:

  1. Connect an external drive to your Windows PC.
  2. Go to File Explorer, right-click on a drive, select Format > exFAT for cross-platform compatibility.
  3. Copy files from Windows to the drive (e.g., drag the Documents folder).
  4. Safely eject the drive from Windows.
  5. Connect the drive to your Mac.
  6. Open Finder, locate the drive, and drag files to your Mac.      

Pros

  • Reliable, works offline
  • Ideal for big data sets

Cons

  • Requires a physical drive
  • Formatting may erase data

Tips 

  1. Use USB-C or Thunderbolt 4 drives for speeds up to 40 Gbps on Mac. 
  2. Verify files after transfer (e.g., open a photo or document). 
  3. Label your drive to avoid confusion. 
  4. Back up the drive before formatting. 
  5. For very large data transfers, consider a fast SSD. 
  6. Once done, keep it as a manual backup. 

5. Network-Attached Storage (NAS)

Best For: Ongoing file access or large-scale transfers

Steps:

  1. Set up your NAS device (e.g., Synology, QNAP) per the manufacturer’s instructions. 
  2. Connect both your Windows PC and Mac to the same network as the NAS. 
  3. On Windows, map the NAS as a network drive (File Explorer > This PC > Map Network Drive). 
  4. Copy files from Windows to the NAS. 
  5. On Mac, open Finder, select Go > Connect to Server and access the NAS (use SMB protocol, e.g., smb://nas-name). 
  6. Move files from the NAS to your Mac. 

Pros

  • Centralized storage for multiple devices
  • Useful for backups and shared access 

Cons

  • Requires NAS hardware
  • Slower on weak networks

Tips

  1. Use wired gigabit Ethernet or 5 GHz Wi-Fi to connect to the NAS for faster transfers. 
  2. Regularly update NAS firmware for compatibility with macOS and Windows. 
  3. Set up user permissions to secure your data. 
  4. Test with a small folder to confirm access. 

6. Use Third-Party Tools

Best For: Power users needing advanced control

Popular Tools: 

  • Carbon Copy Cloner: Creates exact copies of drives (Mac-focused but supports Windows drives). 
  • EaseUS Todo PCTrans: Transfers files, apps, and settings. 
  • AOMEI Backupper: Backs up and restores across platforms. 

Steps:

  1. Install the third-party tool on both Windows and Mac (check compatibility with Windows 11 and macOS Sequoia). 
  2. Follow the tool’s instructions to connect devices (usually via network or direct cable). 
  3. Select files, folders, or entire drives to transfer. 
  4. Monitor the transfer and verify files on the Mac. 

Pros

  • Selective transfer options
  • Some tools clone entire drives

Cons

  • Some features are paid
  • It can be complex for beginners

Tips

  1. Research tools for macOS Sequoia compatibility (check vendor websites). 
  2. Start with free trials to test functionality. 
  3. Back up data before using third-party tools. 
  4. Use trusted software to avoid malware. 

Post-Transfer Checklist

After transferring your files and data from your PC to your Mac, ensure everything is in place: 

  1. Verify Files: Open a few files (e.g., photos, documents) to confirm they transferred correctly and aren’t corrupted. Confirm all important files are present on your Mac. 
  2. Install Apps: Download Mac versions of essential software (e.g., Microsoft Office, Adobe Photoshop) from the Mac App Store or official websites. Also, reconnect printers, scanners, and peripherals. 
  3. Organize Files: Move files to appropriate folders (e.g., Photos to the Photos app, Documents to iCloud Drive).  
  4. Secure Your Mac: Enable FileVault (System Settings > Privacy & Security) to encrypt your data. 
  5. Clean Up: Delete temporary files, eject external drives, or clear cloud storage. 
  6. Update Settings: Reconfigure email accounts, browser bookmarks, or calendar syncs if needed. 

Troubleshooting: Can’t Transfer Data to Mac?

If you hit a snag, try these solutions: 

If issues persist, visit Apple’s support website or contact the tool’s support team. 

Transfer Files to Mac Without the Stress

Migrating from a Windows PC to a Mac doesn’t have to be complicated. Whether you prefer a hands-on approach, such as using an external drive, or an automated one, like Migration Assistant, there’s a solution that fits your needs.

Prepare well, choose your method wisely, and follow through with the checklist. In no time, you’ll be enjoying your new macOS Sequoia setup with all your files intact and ready to go.

  • Affinity vs Photoshop: Canva’s Free Design Suite Tested

title.rendered: Spotify Lossless Audio Is Coming—But What’s the Catch?

content.rendered:
Three years after teasing it, Spotify is finally preparing to roll out lossless audio—and it could arrive through a brand-new subscription tier called Music Pro. While Apple Music users have been enjoying high-fidelity sound at no additional cost, Spotify fans may need to shell out a little extra.

Lossless Audio Code Spotted in Spotify Apps

New evidence uncovered in Spotify’s desktop app, web player, and most recently, its iPhone beta app—points toward the imminent launch of a lossless streaming feature.

These code references suggest Spotify will soon introduce a tier offering “the best sound quality on Spotify: for music in up to 24-bit/44.1 kHz.”

Tech insiders Chris Messina (via TechCrunch), Spicetify (via The Verge), and Aaron Perris (via MacRumors) all independently confirmed the presence of the lossless audio feature buried in Spotify’s code.

What to Expect from Spotify Music Pro

According to a report from Bloomberg’s Lucas Shaw earlier this year, the upcoming Music Pro tier could offer more than just lossless audio. Expected features include:

  • High-fidelity lossless audio
  • DJ-like remixing tools
  • Exclusive access to concert ticket sales

This new tier may cost $5.99 per month in addition to a regular Spotify Premium subscription.

Why the Wait?

Spotify first announced its Hi-Fi tier in 2021, promising audiophile-level sound. But while Apple Music launched its own lossless and hi-res audio offerings later that same year—for free—Spotify’s version quietly disappeared from the spotlight.

Now, with Apple Music raising the bar and YouTube Music also gaining momentum, Spotify is under pressure to finally deliver. But with a rumored surcharge, some users are questioning whether it’s worth the price.

When Will Spotify Lossless Launch?

There’s still no official release date, but the presence of feature-specific code across multiple platforms—especially the iPhone beta app—strongly hints at a 2025 rollout. This aligns with Bloomberg’s earlier report.

Would you pay extra for lossless on Spotify or stick with Apple Music’s free upgrade? Let us know in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: Spotify is finally adding lossless audio—but it may come with a catch. A new “Music Pro” tier could bring hi-fi sound, remix tools, and more at an extra cost.

His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. When not typing away on his MacBook Pro, he loves exploring the real world."

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Apple Faces Lawsuit for $80K Crypto Scam Approved on App Store

content.rendered:
Apple is being sued again. But this time, it’s not about antitrust or developer rules. It’s about trust—the trust Apple promises every time you open the App Store.

A class action lawsuit filed in California accuses Apple of allowing a scam crypto app called Swiftcrypt onto its App Store, which ultimately stole over $80,000 from one user. The case raises serious questions about Apple’s long-standing claims that its App Store is a safe and secure space.

What Happened

In late 2024, Danyell Shin, a marketing and communications professional, downloaded Swiftcrypt from the App Store. It appeared to be a legitimate cryptocurrency trading app. She found it through an online investment group and, trusting Apple’s vetting process, transferred her money in. Then the app froze her account, and her money disappeared. Classic “pig butchering” scam: build trust, drain funds, vanish.

However, this lawsuit doesn’t just target Swiftcrypt. It targets Apple.

Why Apple Is Being Sued

The lawsuit says Apple gave users a false sense of security by branding the App Store as a “safe and trusted” place. Apple has often said that its strict app reviews and anti-fraud checks protect users. The complaint argues that those claims are misleading if scams like Swiftcrypt can still get through.

Shin’s legal team points to:

  • Apple’s own marketing promotes trust and safety
  • Public claims from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook about secure app experiences
  • Apple’s rules require crypto apps to meet licensing and legal standards

According to the lawsuit, Swiftcrypt failed all of that, and Apple let it slide.

More Than Just $80,000

The complaint says Apple didn’t just allow a scam. It profited from the illusion of safety. Even free apps like Swiftcrypt bring value to Apple because the perceived security boosts the value of iPhones.

Shin’s lawyers argue that people overpaid for their iPhones, thinking the App Store was bulletproof. They’re asking for financial compensation for the money lost in the scam (in Shin’s case, over $80,000), as well as for what they claim is the overpayment for iPhones based on misleading App Store safety promises.

They are also asking Apple to run a public campaign to warn the public that not all apps are safe, even on the App Store.

Apple hasn’t responded to the case yet. But this isn’t new territory. The App Store has faced criticism before, notably in the Epic Games lawsuit and a separate $2 billion antitrust case in the UK.

Still, this lawsuit cuts deeper. It strikes at Apple’s core promise: that if an app is on the App Store, it’s been checked and it’s safe.

The Bigger Problem is Brand Value

If Shin’s allegations are true, then Apple failed to stop a fraudulent app from entering a marketplace it alone governs. And that failure comes at a time when Apple is fighting to keep exclusive control over the App Store globally. In the EU, third-party app stores are already allowed, and similar changes may be forced worldwide. Apple has always argued that its single-store model protects user privacy and security. Back in 2021, Craig Federighi even called sideloading a “gold rush for cybercriminals.”

But this lawsuit raises a sharp counterpoint: if fraud is already leaking through Apple’s strict gatekeeping, will users really be safer? Or is the company simply holding on to control because it’s profitable?

When the trust Apple sells breaks, it doesn’t just cost users. It puts Apple’s carefully built image on the line.

title.rendered: 50 Stunning 4K Dynamic Island Wallpapers for iPhone

content.rendered:
If you own an iPhone 16, 15, or 14 Pro, you’re already familiar with the innovative Dynamic Island feature—a clever evolution of the classic notch. But did you know that the right wallpaper can transform your Dynamic Island from a simple cutout into a creative centerpiece? Whether you want to highlight, hide, or playfully incorporate Dynamic Island, the right wallpaper makes all the difference.

In this article, you’ll discover everything you need to know about Dynamic Island wallpapers: what they are, why they matter, how to set them up, and—of course—a handpicked collection of the best HD and 4K options for every style

What Is a Dynamic Island Wallpaper?

Dynamic Island wallpapers are specially designed backgrounds that creatively integrate with the pill-shaped cutout at the top of your iPhone 14 Pro, 15, or 16 display. These wallpapers can:

  • Seamlessly blend the Dynamic Island into the background for a minimalist look.
  • Use playful or artistic elements (like cartoon characters or objects) that interact with the Island.
  • Highlight the notch with gradients, shadows, or bold colors.

The result? Your iPhone’s screen feels more dynamic, personalized, and visually appealing.

Tips for Choosing the Perfect Dynamic Island Wallpaper

  • Personalization: Make your device truly yours by choosing a wallpaper that matches your mood or interests.
  • Creativity: Turn a functional cutout into a fun design element—think cartoon characters hanging from the Island or abstract art that draws the eye.
  • Aesthetic Harmony: Some wallpapers fade or mask the Dynamic Island, making your screen appear sleeker and more unified.
  • Seasonal and Thematic Options: From festive holiday scenes to nostalgic game references, there’s a Dynamic Island wallpaper for every occasion.
  • Consider App Layouts: Some designs work better with certain app arrangements. Minimalist wallpapers often complement busy Home Screens.
  • Try Dark Mode: Wallpapers with dark backgrounds can help the Dynamic Island blend in, especially at night.
Note: Tap the Download button below each wallpaper to save these stunning visuals directly to your iPhone

Best Dynamic Island Wallpapers by Category

                Download

                Shinchan

                Watching Shinchan was and still is an emotional experience! To keep it up, you can download this Shinchan wallpaper that uses Dynamic Island creatively.

                Download

                Wreck-it Ralph

                This vibrant iPhone wallpaper showcases Ralph, the iconic character from Ralph Breaks the Internet, in his signature red plaid shirt and overalls. Perfect for fans of the animated classic, this wallpaper combines playful energy with a modern design.

                Download

                2. Pop Culture & Cartoons Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Wallpapers inspired by iconic movies, TV shows, and beloved cartoon characters—perfect for fans who want to showcase their favorites.

                The Incredibles

                Download

                Classic Muppets (Bert)

                Do you also love the classic Muppets from Sesame Street? Download this wallpaper featuring Bert with his mad expression. The fun part is his iconic straight eyebrows will replace your Dynamic Island, making your iPhone Lock Screen unique.

                Add a splash of humor to your iPhone with this quirky Rick and Morty wallpaper. It features everyone’s favorite mad scientist with his signature drool and unimpressed gaze. I like how the design blends the notch into his eyebrow. Hilarious!

                Channel your inner Saiyan with this pixelated Dragon Ball Z wallpaper for Dynamic Island. Watch as your favorite characters come alive on your screen in pixel-perfect glory.

                3. Superhero Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Spider-Man Upside Down

                The Spider-Man wallpaper for iPhone is sure to serve some quirks on a regular, busy day. While I don’t want you to hang upside down, you can definitely let your Marvel superhero do it from the Dynamic Island.

                Download

                Enjoy this cool Dynamic Island wallpaper featuring your friendly neighborhood superhero, Spider-Man. Feel the thrill on your iPhone screen as Miles Morales swings through Queens, New York.

                Superman

                This one is my personal favorite! If you are also a Marvel fan, you will love this cool Superman wallpaper. The animated look with the vibrant color coming down from the Dynamic Island makes your iPhone one of a kind.

                Batman Dark and Eerie

                Dive into the mysterious world of Batman with this Batman iPhone wallpaper. With a simple tap on the download button, you can capture the dark and eerie air of Gotham City.

                4. Artistic & Abstract Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Creative, visually striking designs with bold colors, gradients, and imaginative patterns for a modern and stylish look.

                Color Gallery

                Immerse yourself in a vibrant spectrum of hues with this beautiful display of color streams. Tap the download button to transform your iPhone into a mesmerizing canvas of color.

                Hot Air Balloon

                Elevate your iPhone experience with this silhouette wallpaper. Gaze upon stunning island vistas while a graceful hot air balloon drifts across the sky. Tap the download button for a scene as inspiring as it is serene!

                Download

                Prism Shadow

                The image of a prism separating light is cliche, but an image of its shadow isn’t. Adding the iPhone’s Dynamic Island to the mix just makes the output spell-bending. Don’t believe us? Download this image and enchant yourselves!

                Download

                Paint Splash

                Crave for something minimalistic yet artistic? Look no further. Quench your creative thirst with Dynamic Island wallpaper brimming with paint.

                Download

                Neon Gradient

                Neon is in vogue! Bring the freshness and vibrancy of neon colors to your iPhone display with this beautiful Dynamic Island wallpaper.

                Download

                Abstract Circles

                Make your iPhone’s Dynamic Island stand out with this bold, abstract design. Circles around the notch add a pop of color to your screen and balance visual impact and minimalism. I like this wallpaper as it effortlessly complements various app layouts.

                Download

                Colorful Rainbow Flow

                This colorful wallpaper features a radiant rainbow flowing from your Dynamic Island. The colors contrast beautifully against the dark background for an eye-catching effect. It’s a perfect choice for expressing personality and vibrancy through your wallpaper.

                Download

                Christmas candy

                Celebrate the holiday season with this Christmas themed iPhone wallpaper. It shows a big candy stick in the middle of a snowy landscape. If you are looking for more festive wallpaper, check out our New Year 2025 wallpaper collection.

                Aesthetic Outdoors

                This aesthetic Dynamic Island wallpaper will infuse your iPhone with a touch of elegance and style. Its captivating design will give your device a unique and eye-catching look. If you’re a fan of the outdoors, tap the download button now!

                Download

                Futuristic Cyberpunk

                Step into the future with this electrifying wallpaper with cyberpunk vibes. Whether you’re a fan of retro-futurism or modern digital art, this wallpaper is sure to turn heads and give your iPhone a distinctive, futuristic edge.

                Download

                Black Stack

                Calling out the black wallpaper lovers! This sleek wallpaper features a mesmerizing pattern of Dynamic Island-shaped pills aligned in a stack. Designed for tech-savvy iPhone users, it provides a minimalist yet high-tech vibe.

                Download

                5. Nature & Scenery Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Serene landscapes, sunsets, and scenic elements that bring a touch of the outdoors and relaxation to your device.

                Summer Sunset

                I don’t know what you did last Summer. But this Summer, you definitely need to have this sunset wallpaper on your iPhone. It’s creative and aspirational at the same time!

                Download

                Speed Boat

                Who doesn’t want to cruise through the waters on a speed boat every day? While that’s not possible for everyone, using this wallpaper is.

                Download

                Ocean View

                If you like the vast blue oceans and sunsets, this wallpaper is ideal. It takes you to a breathtaking coastal landscape. For more stunning options, explore our ocean wallpapers for iPhone and get the beach vibes.

                Download

                Rocket Over Moon

                The rocket might be far from the Moon, and you might be far from your dreams. But let this rocket wallpaper serve as a reminder for you to never stop chasing.

                Download

                Space Escape

                Let’s escape to Space with this iPhone wallpaper. It shows our beautiful planet Earth and an astronaut hanging from your Dynamic Island with a bouquet of sunflowers. How cute it is! If you love cosmic themes, you’ll also enjoy browsing our space wallpapers for iPhone for even more out-of-this-world designs.

                Download

                Hanging Astronaut

                Introducing a unique blend of space and minimalism for your iPhone screen. Enjoy this stunning free download of an astronaut hanging against a background of the cosmos.

                Download

                Spaceship Dream

                Being an astronaut might have been a childhood dream for many. Congratulations if you were able to accomplish it. If you couldn’t, find solace in art by using this wallpaper!

                Download

                Flying Birds

                Display this wallpaper on your iPhone and begin your day with a shot of motivation. Be inspired to spread your wings and fly towards your goals, just like our friends here.

                Download

                6. Nostalgic & Retro Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Wallpapers that evoke classic games and vintage vibes, offering a sense of nostalgia and fun throwbacks.

                Road Rash

                If you’re a 90s gamer, this wallpaper is sure to delight you. Decorate your iPhone with the iconic Road Rash game to experience a quick dose of nostalgia every time you unlock it.

                Download

                Gameboy Classic

                When nostalgia meets modern flair, you get a masterpiece like this. Tap the download button to add a playful, retro vibe to your device with this iPhone Gameboy wallpaper and enhance Dynamic Island’s ever-changing beauty.

                Download

                7. Fun & Playful Dynamic Island Wallpapers

                Lively, quirky, and energetic designs that add a sense of movement and excitement to your Dynamic Island experience.

                Walking Robot

                We are still quite far away from a robot apocalypse. But if the world of robotics fascinates you, you’ll probably enjoy having this wallpaper on your iPhone. I mean, look at those eyes!

                Download

                Flashlight Glow

                Apple recently added the Flashlight indicator to Dynamic Island, which got our team thinking: Why not create a Flashlight wallpaper to celebrate the same? The result was pretty amazing, and we didn’t want to keep it to ourselves.

                Download

                Pinch the Island

                Feel like giving your Dynamic Island a nice little squeeze? Well, doing it yourself might lead you to different apps, so let this image do it for you. 😉

                Download

                Detective

                Nothing misses the eye of a detective. Embody that spirit, gather the confidence, and stride out in style with this iPhone wallpaper.

                Download

                Musical Notes

                Elevate your iPhone’s aesthetics with the finest musical notes. This top-tier wallpaper will make your device stand out with its captivating visuals and vibrant colors.
